children: UK property finance platform's H1 2026 revenue grew 8.6% yr/yr, driven by refinancing activity
Adjusted diluted EPS for H1 2026 rose 1.1%, while basic EPS declined 46.6%
Company proposed interim dividend of 7.9p per share, up 9.7% yr/yr
Company expects 2026 adjusted profit before tax of about £38.0m, up 5% from 2025
Company says market remains refinance-led, with no meaningful recovery in purchase activity expected short term
Mortgage Advice Bureau expects stronger profit contribution from Fluent and improved operating leverage from 2027

REFINANCING ACTIVITY - Co said revenue growth was led by refinancing, particularly Product Transfers, which increased to 27% of lending by value and supported strong activity levels but carried lower revenue contribution than purchase lending
ACQUISITIONS IMPACT - Consolidation of acquisitions completed in 2025 and 2026 contributed to gross profit and margin growth, but also increased administrative expenses
SUBDUED PURCHASE MARKET - Purchase lending reduced by 1% as market conditions remained challenging, with consumer confidence and mortgage pricing volatility affecting demand
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 3 "strong buy" or "buy", no "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the investment management & fund operators peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Mortgage Advice Bureau (Holdings) PLC is GBp1,150.00, about 200.3% above its September 21 closing price of GBp383.00
The stock recently traded at 7 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 9 three months ago
